title: Add RAG agent templates, tool-calling examples, and quickstarts; docs site updates
author: Elliot Marsh
description: Motivation: provide first-class RAG + agent quickstarts and tool-calling examples to help developers integrate Redwood's runtime patterns into production apps. This PR adds: (1) a set of opinionated RAG agent templates (basic, multi-tool, and fallback strategies) under redwood-examples, (2) end-to-end quickstarts for Node/Python that demonstrate tool-calling, structured output, and safe fallback behavior, (3) docs site pages and sidebar entries with walkthroughs, screenshots, and runnable snippets, and (4) small CI e2e tests for the quickstarts. Checklist: - [x] Add example templates and starter manifests - [x] Add Node + Python quickstart samples with READMEs - [x] Update docs site navigation and quickstart pages - [x] Add e2e test harness for quickstarts - [x] Run CI and fix lint/test failures Notes: examples are intentionally opinionated to demonstrate recommended defaults (prefix caching enabled, streaming with chunking, tool call schema examples). The docs page includes migration notes for customers moving from single-model RAG to agent-based tool-calling (see linked Linear ENG-2148). This is a docs + examples focused change; there are no runtime behavior changes to the serving layer. Related: redwood-examples PR will be mirrored to the examples repo; maintainers should watch the redwood-examples release pipeline for the package publish step. CI history: initial CI run showed lint failures on docs markdown: fixed in commit 2; e2e flakiness addressed by adding retries and increasing timeouts in the test harness. Merge strategy: squash and merge to keep changelog compact.
